# pulumi/pulumi

**Pulumi IaC: infrastructure as code in any programming language.**

[Pulumi IaC](https://www.pulumi.com/product/infrastructure-as-code/) is an open-source infrastructure as code tool for creating, deploying, and managing cloud infrastructure on any cloud. Write your infrastructure in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, C#, Java, or YAML, and use the loops, functions, classes, testing tools, and package managers you already know.

## About this image

The "kitchen sink" image: the Pulumi CLI with every supported language and a set of common cloud tools, ready to run any Pulumi program. It's about 2 GB. If you only use one language, the slim images for each language are much smaller, at 200 to 300 MB. See [the full list of images](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers#images).

It contains:

- The Pulumi CLI, all Pulumi language runtimes, and the OPA policy analyzer.
- Node.js 22, 24, and 26 (default 26), managed by [fnm](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm), with npm, Yarn, pnpm, Bun, and Corepack.
- Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 (default 3.13), managed by [pyenv](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv), with pip, Poetry, and uv.
- Go 1.26.10.
- .NET SDK 8.0, 9.0, and 10.0.
- OpenJDK 21.
- Cloud and container tools: the AWS CLI, `aws-iam-authenticator`, the Azure CLI, the Google Cloud CLI with the GKE auth plugin, `kubectl`, Helm, and the Docker CLI.

## Tags and platforms

Each Pulumi release is published under these tags, where `<version>` is the Pulumi CLI version, for example `3.200.0`:

| Tag | Runs as | Platforms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<version>`, `latest` | `root` | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` |
| `<version>-amd64` | `root` | `linux/amd64` |
| `<version>-arm64` | `root` | `linux/arm64` |
| `<version>-nonroot`, `latest-nonroot` | `pulumi` (UID 1000) | `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` |
| `<version>-nonroot-amd64` | `pulumi` (UID 1000) | `linux/amd64` |
| `<version>-nonroot-arm64` | `pulumi` (UID 1000) | `linux/arm64` |

The image is based on Debian 13 (trixie). Tags without an architecture suffix are multi-platform manifest lists, so `docker pull` selects the right image for your machine.

## Usage

The image's entrypoint is `pulumi`, so pass the Pulumi command as arguments:

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN \
  -v "$(pwd)":/pulumi/projects \
  -w /pulumi/projects \
  pulumi/pulumi \
  preview
```

Pass the credentials for your cloud provider as environment variables, too.

## Choosing a language version

The `pulumi/pulumi` image includes several versions of Node.js, Python, and .NET. By default, it uses Node.js 26 and Python 3.13. How you select another version depends on the language.

### Node.js

The image uses [fnm](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm) to manage Node.js versions, and comes with the latest patch releases of Node.js 22, 24, and 26 installed. To select a version, create a `.node-version` file in your project directory with the version you want, then run `pulumi install --use-language-version-tools`. This sets up the aliases for Node.js, npm, and the other Node.js tools in `/usr/local/share/fnm/aliases/default/bin`.

To avoid downloading Node.js on every run, specify only the major version, for example `26`. This ensures that the preinstalled version is used.

If you're building your own image from `pulumi/pulumi`, run `fnm alias <version> default` to change the default version of Node.js in your image.

### Python

The image uses [pyenv](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv) to manage Python versions, and comes with Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 installed. To select a version, create a `.python-version` file in your project directory with the version you want.

To avoid downloading and building Python on every run, specify only the minor version, for example `3.13`. This ensures that the preinstalled version is used.

### .NET

The image includes the .NET SDK 8.0, 9.0, and 10.0. The `TargetFramework` property in your project's `.csproj` or `.fsproj` file determines which one is used:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    ...
```

### Go

The `go` directive in your project's `go.mod` file determines the version of Go used to build your program. See [Go toolchains](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain).

### Java

The image includes a single version of the JDK, OpenJDK 21.

## Registries

Every image is published to Docker Hub, the AWS ECR Public Gallery, and the GitHub Container Registry.

| Image | Docker Hub | ECR Public | GHCR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pulumi/pulumi` | [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/pulumi/pulumi) | [ECR Public](https://gallery.ecr.aws/pulumi/pulumi) | [GHCR](https://github.com/orgs/pulumi/packages/container/package/pulumi) |

For example, `docker pull pulumi/pulumi`, `docker pull public.ecr.aws/pulumi/pulumi`, or `docker pull ghcr.io/pulumi/pulumi`.

## Releases

Images are built and published automatically for every release of the [Pulumi CLI](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/releases), usually once a week, with patch releases in between when needed. Image tags match the version of the Pulumi CLI they contain. For example, when Pulumi `v3.200.0` is released, it's published as `3.200.0`. The `latest` tag always points to the most recent release.

To avoid unexpected upgrades, pin your image to a specific version tag rather than `latest`.

Images are scanned nightly for vulnerabilities. We remediate findings where we can, on a best-effort basis. Some findings, such as vulnerabilities in base images with no available fix, are outside our control.

## Getting help

- Problems with an image, such as a missing tool, a vulnerability, or a broken tag: [open an issue in pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-docker-containers/issues/new).
- Problems with the Pulumi CLI or SDKs: [open an issue in pulumi/pulumi](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues/new/choose).
- Questions: ask in the [Pulumi Community Slack](https://slack.pulumi.com/).
